{{short description|Australian biologist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Patrick Ping Leung Tam''' ({{zh|t=譚秉亮}}} is an Australian embryologist currently at [[University of Sydney]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cmri.org.au/About-Us/Lead-Researchers/Patrick-Tam |title=Patrick Tam |publisher=cmri.org.au |accessdate=November 27, 2017}}</ref> the Deputy Director of the Childrens Medical Research institute,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sbs.com.au/yourlanguage/cantonese/en/audiotrack/celebrity-chatroom-professor-patrick-tam |title=Celebrity Chatroom |publisher=sbs.com.au |accessdate=November 27, 2017}}</ref> the Distinguished Professor and Mok Hing-Yiu Distinguished Visiting Professor at [[University of Hong Kong]].

He is a cited pioneer in his field for studying mouse embryos, cells and biology.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&as_sdt=0%2C44&q=Patrick+Tam&btnG= |title=Patrick Tam |accessdate=November 27, 2017}}</ref>

Tam is a member of the editorial board for numerous journals relating to developmental biology; including [[Developmental Biology (journal)|Developmental Biology]], [[Developmental Cell]], [[Developmental Dynamics]], [[Differentiation (journal)|Differentiation]] and [[Genesis (journal)|Genesis]]. He has also served as a guest editor on other publications.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Patrick Tam |url=https://croucher.org.hk/en/fellows-and-scholars/tam-ping-leung-patrick |access-date=2025-09-24 |website=Croucher Foundation |language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and fellowships ==

* In 2007 he received the President’s Medal from the Australia and New Zealand Society of Cell and Developmental Biology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=President's Medal |url=https://www.anzscdb.org/presidents-medal-1 |access-date=2025-09-24 |website=Australia and New Zealand Society of Cell and Developmental Biology. |language=en-AU}}</ref>
* He is an elected fellow of the [[Institute of Biology]], [[Australian Academy of Science]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows |url=https://www.science.org.au/fellowship/fellows/professor-patrick-ping-leung-tam |accessdate=November 27, 2017 |publisher=science.org.au}}</ref> [[Australian Academy of Health and Medical Sciences]], [[Royal Society of Biology]] and the [[Royal Society of London]] (2001).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Patrick Tam |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/patrick-tam-12383/ |accessdate=November 27, 2017 |publisher=royalsociety.org}}</ref><ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Patrick Tam |url=http://sydney.edu.au/medicine/people/academics/profiles/patrick.tam.php |accessdate=November 27, 2017 |publisher=sydney.edu.au}}</ref>

==Publications==
*SOX9 directly regulates the type-ll collagen gene, Nature, 1997
*SOX9 binds DNA, activates transcription, and coexpresses with type II collagen during chondrogenesis in the mouse, Elsevier, 1997
*Depletion of definitive gut [[endoderm]] in Sox17-null mutant mice, 2002, dev.biologists.org
*Mouse gastrulation: the formation of a mammalian body plan, Elsevier, 1997
*Gene function in mouse embryogenesis: get set for gastrulation, Nature Reviews, 2007
